title: Portfolio Assistant LLM Defense
description: Interview defense for a custom retrieval-based portfolio chatbot using FastAPI, TF-IDF, ONNX MiniLM embeddings, query rules, artifacts, training data, evaluation, Docker, and caveats.

questions.prompt: What is the production endpoint for the portfolio chatbot?
questions.explanation: The FastAPI backend exposes /, /health, and POST /chat. /chat calls answer_from_messages() for production chatbot behavior.

concept_panel.title: Portfolio Chat API
concept_panel.explanation: The FastAPI backend exposes /, /health, and POST /chat. /chat calls answer_from_messages() for production chatbot behavior.
concept_panel.practical_example: A frontend sends messages to POST /chat and receives a portfolio-specific answer.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you know your deployed API flow.

questions.prompt: What does the chat request send?
options: A messages array with role/content plus request metadata
Only a raw string file path
questions.answer: A messages array with role/content plus request metadata
questions.explanation: The schema accepts chat messages, and the backend finds the latest user message before answering.

concept_panel.title: Request Schema
concept_panel.explanation: The schema accepts chat messages, and the backend finds the latest user message before answering.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand request modeling.

questions.prompt: What is the production chatbot model?
options: A direct OpenAI API call only
questions.explanation: The live model maps user queries to trained portfolio Q&A targets using lexical and optional semantic retrieval.

concept_panel.title: Production Model Type
concept_panel.explanation: The live model maps user queries to trained portfolio Q&A targets using lexical and optional semantic retrieval.
concept_panel.practical_example: answer_from_messages() searches trained examples and returns the best target_text.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you can distinguish production architecture from experiments.

questions.prompt: What does the lexical part use?
options: TF-IDF cosine similarity over normalized tokens
questions.answer: TF-IDF cosine similarity over normalized tokens
questions.explanation: TF-IDF gives strong keyword-based retrieval and is easy to inspect/debug.

concept_panel.title: TF-IDF Lexical Matching
concept_panel.explanation: TF-IDF gives strong keyword-based retrieval and is easy to inspect/debug.
concept_panel.practical_example: A query mentioning 'GitHub' can match portfolio examples containing GitHub-related terms.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand classic IR foundations.

questions.prompt: What adds semantic matching if enabled?
questions.explanation: The semantic path uses MiniLM embeddings from ONNX artifacts when enabled and available.

concept_panel.title: Semantic Matching
concept_panel.explanation: The semantic path uses MiniLM embeddings from ONNX artifacts when enabled and available.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand local embedding-based retrieval.

questions.prompt: Why include aliases and follow-up expansion?
options: To normalize user intent before retrieval
questions.answer: To normalize user intent before retrieval
questions.explanation: Rules handle common terms such as github/resume and vague follow-ups like 'tell me more'.

concept_panel.title: Query Rules
concept_panel.explanation: Rules handle common terms such as github/resume and vague follow-ups like 'tell me more'.
concept_panel.practical_example: Map 'his backend work' to Hisham backend portfolio context.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you can improve retrieval UX without an external LLM.

questions.prompt: Why rewrite first-person answers into third person?
options: To match questions asking about Hisham or his work
questions.answer: To match questions asking about Hisham or his work
questions.explanation: The assistant can adapt answer perspective so portfolio content sounds natural to visitors.

concept_panel.title: Third-Person Rewriting
concept_panel.explanation: The assistant can adapt answer perspective so portfolio content sounds natural to visitors.
concept_panel.practical_example: Convert 'I built Forecast Alpha' into 'Hisham built Forecast Alpha'.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you notice product polish around generated responses.

questions.prompt: When should the assistant return 'I'm still learning that part...'?
options: When retrieval confidence is below threshold or topic is unknown
questions.answer: When retrieval confidence is below threshold or topic is unknown
questions.explanation: A deterministic fallback is safer than hallucinating unsupported portfolio claims.

concept_panel.title: Fallback Behavior
concept_panel.explanation: A deterministic fallback is safer than hallucinating unsupported portfolio claims.
concept_panel.practical_example: Unknown personal questions should not produce invented biography.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand safe AI behavior.

options: portfolio_retriever.json, portfolio_embeddings.npz, and ONNX MiniLM config
questions.answer: portfolio_retriever.json, portfolio_embeddings.npz, and ONNX MiniLM config
questions.explanation: The production retriever loads trained lexical data and optional semantic embeddings/model config.

concept_panel.title: Runtime Artifacts

options: Supervised portfolio Q&A examples for retrieval training

options: An isolated research experiment, not the production /chat retriever
questions.answer: An isolated research experiment, not the production /chat retriever

concept_panel.explanation: The generative BiLSTM encoder/decoder with attention is experimental and should not replace production retrieval without evaluation.

questions.prompt: What is the important test caveat?
options: Tests import backend.model.inference while live API imports model.portfolio_llm
questions.answer: Tests import backend.model.inference while live API imports model.portfolio_llm
questions.explanation: Current tests cover API/training/inference basics, dataset cleaning, and tokenization, but do not fully exercise the deployed chat behavior.

concept_panel.title: Tests and Caveat
concept_panel.explanation: Current tests cover API/training/inference basics, dataset cleaning, and tokenization, but do not fully exercise the deployed chat behavior.
concept_panel.practical_example: Add a test that POST /chat exercises answer_from_messages() from model/portfolio_llm.py.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you can honestly identify coverage gaps.

coding_challenges.title: Portfolio Assistant LLM Defense status classifier
coding_challenges.instructions: Implement classify_status_code(code: int) -> str. Return success for 200-299, redirect for 300-399, client_error for 400-499, server_error for 500-599, and unknown otherwise.
coding_challenges.explanation: The challenge reinforces deterministic branching, status-code categories, and local test execution.
